headline: Requests for speed humps on several streets and a traffic light at Todd Street and Whitney Avenue.
summary: Several residents ask for speed humps or other traffic-calming steps on their streets. Another asks for a traffic light at Todd Street and Whitney Avenue, and two road races also need approval.
items: Request to approve the Cheshire Half Marathon on April 11, 2027
Request to approve the New Haven Road Race on 9/6/27
Request for speed humps on Bradley Avenue
Request for speed bumps on West Shepard Avenue
Traffic-calming request on Augur Street or speed hump installation
Request for a traffic light at Todd Street and Whitney Avenue
Request for slow-down and children-at-play signs near the park on Noble Street
Traffic-calming requests and possible traffic study on Riverside Drive
Executive session, if recommended by the town attorney
location: 3rd Floor Conference Room, Hamden Government Center, 2750 Dixwell Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518; also on Zoom
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
TRAFFIC AUTHORITY 
 
REGULAR MEETING AGENDA 
 
5:30 PM, NOVEMBER 9, 2026 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
3rd Floor Conference Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 
Meeting Agenda: The Traffic Authority, Town of Hamden, will hold a hybrid Regular 
Meeting on Monday, November 9, 2026 at 5:30 PM at the Hamden Government Center, 
3rd Floor conference room and virtually on Zoom. 
  
Please click the link below to join the webinar: 
https://hamden.zoom.us/j/87107298379   
Webinar ID: 87107298379 | By Phone: +1 312 626 6799   
Comments for this meeting agenda can be heard by joining the meeting in person or via zoom 
and participating in the public input session, or you can write in and send them to 
nforvil@gmail.com by 3:00 PM of the meeting date. If you send a comment in, you can still 
speak during the Public Input Session. 
 
To participate in public input live you must: 
 
1. Have your name displayed on your screen. 
2. Raise your hand to speak when the public input session is opened (You will be called upon in 
the order that your hand is raised).  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
 
2. ATTENDANCE 
 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
 
  a. Approval of minutes of the Traffic Authority's regular meetings on October 19, 2026. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.  
  a. John Bysiewicz, 2 Bueno Vista Road- Seeking LTA approval for the Cheshire Half 
Marathon on April 11, 2027 to include with our DOT special event permit. The Half 
Marathon runs into Hamden. The course has not changed from year's past. We will 
hire Hamden police officers to be along the course. 
 
  b. John Bysiewicz, 2 Buena Vista Road — Seeking LTA approval for the New Haven 
Road Race on 9/6/27 to include with our DOT special event permit. The Half 
Marathon runs into Hamden. The course has not changed from year's past. We will 
hire Hamden police officers to be along the course. 
  c. Craig Cherry, 20 Bradley Ave — Requesting speed humps on the street.  
  d. Teresa A. Lupi Elissa Lupi, 85 W Shepard Ave — The West Shepard Neighborhood 
is petitioning the Town of Hamden's Traffic Authority to construct speed bumps along 
our road to slow down the speed of vehicles. 
 
Our street begins at Shepard Ave with the Laurel Oaks School, continuing past 
Laurel View Golf Course, and The VUE restaurant/venue. There are hills, curves, 
blind spots, and no sidewalks. 
Numerous college students living along the West Shepard Ave, Laura Rd and Hill St 
corridor travel our street daily to get to and from Quinnipiac University. 
 
Along with loud, racing vehicles appearing out of nowhere, at all times of the day and 
night, causing neighbors to take notice. We also have large delivery trucks, golfers 
and partiers anxious to get to their next destination, especially during the warm 
weather months. We have met with police concerning the traffic, and at this point, we 
want to be preventative and not wait for a serious incident to occur. Please consider 
our request for speed bumps to ensure everyone’s safety. 
6. REPORTS 
 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney) 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
 
  a. John Murphy, 253 Augur Street — Traffic-calming request on Augur Street or speed 
hump installation, the stop sign is ignored by motorists. 
  b. Dorette Fowlin, 50 Bradley Avenue — Neighborhood concerns about speeding in 
general on a regular basis. Dog was killed, cars have been damaged (hit & run) and a 
child was struck between Duane Street and Bradley Avenue. School is close by and 
many children walk or ride bicycles to school because the bus doesn't pick up on 
Bradley Avenue due to proximity to the school (Helen Street School). Speed humps 
on the roadway would go a long way on slowing down the motorists. 
  c. Marylou Weinzimmer — I am writing to formally request the installation of a traffic 
light on the corner of Todd Street and Whitney Avenue. This intersection experiences
heavy traffic throughout the day, especially work traffic. It is impossible in the morning 
and late afternoon to take a left onto Whitney. As one side clears, the other side fills 
up, and you are just in a holding pattern with cars piling up on Todd Street. I also feel 
this will slow traffic down, especially during school season, as the students from 
Quinnipiac are trying to cross and walk on Whitney, which is obviously so dangerous 
and unsafe for all. Thank you for your consideration and I look forward to hearing a 
response. 
  d. SILDA NOLASCO, 80 NOBLE ST—I am writing as a resident of 80 Noble Street in 
Hamden to bring an important traffic and pedestrian safety concern to your attention 
regarding the park located directly in front of my home. Since moving to this 
residence, I have become increasingly concerned about the speed at which some 
vehicles travel through this area. The entrance to the park and the street are very 
close to one another, and children frequently run, walk, and play in and around the 
park. At times, I have personally observed vehicles traveling fast enough that drivers 
have had to stop suddenly when children were near or crossing the street. Because 
the park is used by children and families, I believe additional traffic-safety measures 
could help make the area safer. 
 
I respectfully ask the Town to consider installing slow-down signs, children-at-play 
signs, pedestrian crossing signs, or other appropriate traffic-control measures near 
the park to alert drivers that they are entering an area where children and pedestrians 
are frequently present. I am also concerned about the number of vehicles that remain 
parked in the area for extended periods, including while children and families are 
using the park. The park includes a public restroom, and some individuals appear to 
use the area for extended periods, including sleeping in their vehicles. This has made 
some parents and families uncomfortable while bringing their children to the park. I 
understand that the park is a public space and that everyone has the right to use it.  
 
My concern is primarily the safety and comfort of the children and families who use 
the park, particularly because the street and park entrance are so close together. As 
a parent and a new resident of the neighborhood, I find it difficult to feel comfortable 
allowing my children to play at the park or cross the street to access it when vehicles 
are traveling at high speeds. A public park intended for children should be a place 
where families can feel safe and comfortable. I respectfully ask the Town of Hamden 
to please evaluate this area and consider whether additional signage, traffic-calming 
measures, pedestrian safety improvements, or increased enforcement may be 
appropriate. I believe taking preventive action now could help avoid a serious 
accident or injury in the future. Thank you for taking the time to consider my concerns 
and for helping make our neighborhood safer for children, families, pedestrians, and 
drivers. I would greatly appreciate any assistance or information regarding what steps 
can be taken to address this situation. 
  e. Jennie Ragan — We are wondering if there was any further information about traffic-
calming requests in the town. We have lived on Riverside Drive since 2014. Over the 
course of that time, the speeding coming directly down Riverside Drive and off of the 
side streets has gotten progressively worse. We’ve come to the point where we are 
very hesitant to even take a walk with our children on bikes or scooters in the 
neighborhood because of how fast the traffic has become. We are very concerned 
that there is going to be an accident and somebody is going to get hurt and have 
personally had close calls with speeding vehicles. We think the road would be a very 
good candidate for a traffic study and imagine we’d be able to get the required
number of signatures if submission was still allowed or would be considered on a 
case by case basis. Please let us know if you have any further information on how we 
might be able to improve the safety in the neighborhood. 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
 
  
NOTE: The public may address any item on the agenda of a regular or special meeting and any 
matter within the purview of a Board or Commission at a regular meeting either electronically or 
in person, unless otherwise set forth or constrained by Law of the provisions of this Charter.
